title: Permanent anticoncentration for complex Gaussian matrices
source: Aaronson and Arkhipov state this as Conjecture~6 in Section~1.2.3 of their arXiv version \sourcecite{ref:pacc-aa}{AA13}.
progress:
The earlier Theorem~54 of Aaronson and Arkhipov gives only
$\Pr[|\operatorname{Per}X|^2\geq\theta n!]>(1-\theta)^2/(n+1)$ for $0<\theta<1$.
That moment argument guarantees a fraction of large values; it does not alone control the small-value tail \sourcecite{ref:pacc-aa}{AA13}.

references.label: ref:pacc-aa
references.tex: S. Aaronson and A. Arkhipov, "The Computational Complexity of Linear Optics," \emph{Theory of Computing} \textbf{9}(4), 143--252 (2013). \href{https://doi.org/10.4086/toc.2013.v009a004}{doi:10.4086/toc.2013.v009a004}; \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.3245}{arXiv:1011.3245}.

references.label: ref:pacc-kl
references.tex: F. Koehler and P. K. Leung, "Anticoncentration of the Permanent in Ginibre Ensembles," arXiv preprint (2026). \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20329v1}{arXiv:2607.20329v1}.

comment:
The archived anticoncentration question is resolved by a preprint; no journal publication is asserted.
It is distinct from the Permanent-of-Gaussians hardness conjecture.
Combining this result with Aaronson--Arkhipov Theorem~7 makes their additive squared-permanent and multiplicative permanent estimation tasks polynomial-time equivalent \sourcecite{ref:pacc-aa}{AA13}.
It does not prove either task hard.
